justification: Arguing each: A fails because no price for drying is ever given (only “at so much per ton per point of moisture” in passing); B names one thread only — Grendisham’s “On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window” — not the whole; C is absent. The text opens on a settled rule, “the tall machine with the ducts inside is the one that burns” and “The explanation is as settled as the count,” then gives most of its length to Calverend, Grendisham and Steadgrove disagreeing about why. D captures both halves exactly.

The swab result is stated once: “per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent.” That kills A (reverses it) and C (nothing is said about new ducts being clean; the sample was “twenty-six machines that had never burned”). D fails because nobody in the passage attacks the sample — Steadgrove “accepts the swabs” and the writer says “The swabs are hard to walk past.” B is the plain reading.

Grendisham’s point is about what the second timestamp records: “The other time in the file is the moment the call came in... that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught,” and “It looks late because nobody was there to see it early.” A is the opposite of her claim that the two numbers only look aligned when “Set those two numbers side by side”; B and D are never said — she disputes the reading of the times, not their coverage or purpose. C.

Steadgrove’s date-sort is the source: “Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine, and the machine stops mattering,” with “Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest, when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator’s delivery window is closing.” B is contradicted by the arithmetic (forty-nine of sixty-one, not every fire); C overreaches beyond anything claimed, and the writer notes Steadgrove’s remedy “is not the mutual’s to give”; D (grain arriving faster than dryers can take it) is never stated. A is what “the machine stops mattering” implies — the same commercial squeeze regardless of equipment.

The writer states her position outright in the last paragraph: “Until then Calverend’s account fits the evidence without having been tested by it,” preceded by “Grendisham’s objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these.” A is excluded by that same sentence, B by the fact that she does adjudicate (“The swabs are hard to walk past”), and D by “nobody has worked out how to check” before next harvest. C.

Gap (1) completes a fixed collocation, “to take the long ___,” after “which puts the bottom of the list twelve years from a key” — i.e. accept a long-term perspective. Only “view” forms that idiom; “take the long outlook/gaze/sight” are not English collocations, and “gaze” and “sight” are literal looking. C.

Gap (2) heads a rule-as-written statement that the next sentences set against practice: “That is the clause as written, and nobody disputes it or finds it odd. It is simply not what the list runs on.” “Strictly” (strictly speaking, by the rule) is exactly that move. “Curiously” is blocked by “nobody... finds it odd”; “Increasingly” asserts a trend the passage never gives; “Privately” contradicts a written clause. B.

Gap (3) is inside a named idiom — “The older hands have a phrase for this among themselves, about waiting for dead men’s ___” — and the only phrase in English is “dead men’s shoes,” waiting for a place that falls vacant on a death. It matches the surrounding sense: “Movement comes when somebody else stops... a winter that settles it,” and “It is not affectionate and it is not quite a joke.” Coats, gloves and hats form no such phrase. A.

Gap (4) sits in a two-pole concession: “the tone of that line is not approving, but it is not ___ either,” so the gap needs the opposite pole of approving. “Censorious” supplies it; “gracious” sits on the approving side and makes the contrast collapse, while “cautious” and “anxious” are not opposites of approval at all. The context — a tenancy quietly passing to a nephew, given “one line” in the minutes — is the committee neither blessing nor condemning. D.

Gap (5) takes a rule as object: “The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list. The rule has not been ___.” Rules are invoked; the point is that after “Three times the answer was no” the rule was never applied. “Summoned” takes people, “provoked” takes reactions, and “evoked” takes memories or feelings — the near-homophone trap. C.

The passage says height, not pattern, carries information: “The pot that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack.” That is A. B is contradicted by the stated reason for a narrow mouth — “since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening” (rain and birds are never mentioned); C by “Pattern tells you very little”; D by “Builders’ yards sold whatever was in stock” and “a stack rebuilt in 1961 carries what came off the lorry.”

The figures are the whole item: the chandler’s hatch “opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller’s opened at two and took in 390,” and “Both shut when the evening cart went at eight” — thirteen hours against six for twenty-two more letters. That kills B (412 vs 390 is not “far more”) and C (both shut at eight, so the bookseller stayed open after nothing). A is the strongest near-miss, since the keeper “was allowed threepence for every hour the hatch stood open, and not a penny for the letters themselves,” but it says “the keepers” stretched their hours and the bookseller “opened at two” — a six-hour day — so it is not supported for both. D is what the near-equal counts against unequal hours imply.

The sequence is given in order: “Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten, när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan”, “fick ligga ute vintern över” and “Först därefter rostades den”. A inverts both the season and the order (roasting before the heap); B is contradicted by “Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt”; D by “Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte”. C restates the passage.

The first of Tolvsäter’s two results is explicit: “De blåsningar som drevs hårdast, med tätare bälgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet, och klumpen sprack under släggan” — harder driving, more carbon in the metal, more brittle. B reverses it; C overstates it into total failure, which the text never says; D is not a result of the trials — drying is mentioned only in the description of the furnace itself. A.

The solid-state reduction is named as the root of the rest: “Järnet reducerades i fast form”, “Ur detta följer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom”, “En blåsning gav några kilo järn” and “Tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efteråt” — both lupp size and where the work sat. A fails on the dating, “Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket till tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet”; B reverses the two technologies, since it was the hytta that “krävde vattenkraft”; C is contradicted by “uppteckningarna... säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen”. D.

Tolvsäter’s second result answers this directly: “den järnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lägre järnhalt blir trögflytande vid de temperaturer en sådan ugn orkar hålla... Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet.” A is Krokvall’s reading of “dålig kontroll”, which the trials speak against; C is contradicted by “i flera fall kring en tredjedel” and by dating resting on charcoal; D is excluded by “varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen”. B.

The writer withdraws her vote but not the need: “Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst” against “Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga”, closing with “Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten” — equipment yes, fee-funding no. B is contradicted by the cut line, the short ladder and the absent defibrillator; C by the retraction; A by the fact that her objection is to the mechanism, not the level (“Avgiften vid bryggan lär förskjuta en del av badandet just dit”). D.

The one figure given is “Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna” — so roughly sixty-nine per cent, about seven nights in ten, went unpaid. C inverts it; B is contradicted by the fact that the follow-up produced a number at all; D is never mentioned — the sign is described as still the model (“en skylt, en kod och tilliten till att gästen skannar”). A.

What the anmälningar showed is stated plainly: “I de fall där skriften gick att jämföra med annat i mappen härrörde yrkesordet i regel från abonnenten själv.” A is the opposite of that; C is contradicted by “Titelraden var tom på den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista över godkända ord”; B goes past the evidence, since the text says the strikeouts “kan lika gärna vara ändrade beslut som rättelser av en felläsning – materialet svarar inte på det”. D.

She concedes: “Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså. Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt, och den förklaring som från början låg närmast är också den som står kvar” — and that nearest explanation was the ordinary one, “Den förklaring som ligger närmast är fåfänga.” A is contradicted by “Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt”; D by “Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns”, which leaves nothing to combine; C overreads the residue — “Ett par saker får jag ändå inte att gå ihop” concerns loose details, not the main question, which she does settle. B.

The passage states the digging season and the sequence explicitly: "Arbetet gjordes sent på hösten, när vattnet i mossen hade sjunkit undan. Malmen grävdes upp i smala rutor, lades i högar på fastare mark och fick ligga ute vintern över ... Först därefter rostades den" — late autumn, a winter outdoors, roasting last, which is C. A inverts both the season and the order (spring frost, roasting before stacking) and is doubly contradicted by "Först därefter rostades den". B is refuted by "Långt ifrån varje mosse bär ett sådant skikt", and D by "Utan spettet gick skiktet inte att finna, för på ytan syns det inte" — wetness is why the work waited for low water, never a substitute for the spett.

The trial result is stated as a mechanism: "De blåsningar som drevs hårdast, med tätare bälgtag och mer kol i varven, gav inte större luppar utan sprödare: kolet gick in i järnet, och klumpen sprack under släggan" — harder driving, more carbon in the metal, brittler iron: A. B reverses the direction of the finding. C overstates it into total failure, which the text never says — the hard runs produced lumps, they were merely brittle. D transplants the drying advice from the furnace paragraph ("måste den torkas långsamt") into Tolvsäter's results, where the text reports only two findings, neither about masonry or drying.

The passage makes solid-state reduction the hinge of everything else: "Det är hantverkets utgångspunkt. Järnet reducerades i fast form ... Ur detta följer mycket av det som annars ser ut som fattigdom. En blåsning gav några kilo järn ... Tyngdpunkten i arbetet låg inte vid ugnen utan i smedjan efteråt" — both lump size and where the labour sat, i.e. D. B reverses the two technologies: it is the later hytta that "krävde vattenkraft och ständig drift". C is contradicted head-on by "uppteckningarna, som är utförliga om vem som ägde vad, säger nästan ingenting om själva blåsningen". A is the subtlest miss: cheap building is real ("Ugnen kostade lera, sten och ved"), but the dating sentence "Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket till tiden mellan 300-talet och 1200-talet" puts the practice centuries before the 1800s, and the 1880s records concern ore regrowth and ownership, not live smelting.

Tolvsäter's second result licenses exactly one inference: "den järnrika slaggen visade sig vara ett villkor. En slagg med lägre järnhalt blir trögflytande vid de temperaturer en sådan ugn orkar hålla ... Järnet i avfallet är priset för att slaggen alls ska lämna schaktet" — B. A is Krokvall's reading of the same numbers ("ett tecken på dålig kontroll"), and the text closes it off: "det är tolkningen av dem som försöken talar emot". C fails twice — the iron ran "i flera fall kring en tredjedel", not uniformly, and dating comes from charcoal ("Kolet ur tappgroparna daterar bruket"). D is blocked by the explicit ignorance claim "varken malmens halt eller ugnarnas mått räcker för att förklara spridningen".

The writer withdraws her vote while conceding the need: "Nu vill jag ta tillbaka min röst", "Att åtgärder behövs är ingen stridsfråga", and her closing prescription "Köp bojarna, badstegen och hjärtstartaren över driftsbudgeten" — equipment yes, fee no, i.e. D. B is refuted by the same "ingen stridsfråga" sentence plus the cut boj line and the stege that "slutar en halvmeter ovanför vattenytan". C is what she voted for and now retracts. A is the trap for a careless reader: she attacks the calculation ("Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent") to show fees will not collect, never to argue for a larger sum.

The only figure given for the ställplats is "Kommunens egen uppföljning landade på en betalningsgrad om 31 procent av gästnätterna" — 69 per cent unpaid, which A renders as roughly seven nights in ten. C states the arithmetic opposite. B is contradicted by the fact that the municipality did measure it and reported a number. D imports an outcome the text never mentions: the sign, code and open grind are described as still standing ("en grind som står öppen hela säsongen"), and the writer's point is that the same design would work even worse at the bryggan.

The archive finding is stated plainly: "I de fall där skriften gick att jämföra med annat i mappen härrörde yrkesordet i regel från abonnenten själv" — D, hedge and all. A is the kassör hypothesis she abandons ("Ingen av mina tre mekanismer fanns alltså"). C is refuted by "Titelraden var tom på den tryckta blanketten: ingen lista över godkända ord, ingen anvisning om längd". B is the strongest wrong answer because the twenty-odd strikeovers are real, but the text refuses precisely that reading: "överstrykningarna kan lika gärna vara ändrade beslut som rättelser av en felläsning — materialet svarar inte på det".

She concedes: "Jag får ge Rämnestad rätt, och den förklaring som från början låg närmast är också den som står kvar" — the nearest explanation being "fåfänga", so she drops her own suspicion for the ordinary account: B. A is contradicted by "Där hade jag fel" and by the concession itself. D invents a both-and settlement the text never offers; she reports that none of her three mechanisms existed. C is the tempting near-miss, since "Ett par saker får jag ändå inte att gå ihop" — but those are named residuals (the hemmansägare, the widows, the strikeovers), not a refusal to decide the main question, which she does decide.

The text opens on a settled rule — "the mixed-flow has a fixed reputation: the tall machine with the ducts inside is the one that burns" — and then spends four paragraphs on rival accounts of why (Calverend's shutdown timing, Grendisham's clock objection, Steadgrove's contract), which is D. A is absent: the per-ton-per-point charge appears once as background, never tracked over nine harvests. B names Grendisham's single objection, one move inside the dispute rather than its subject; C is not raised at all — custom drying is described, never recommended against.

The swab result is quantified as a non-difference: "per square foot the mixed-flow dryers carried what the cross-flow columns carried, within a few percent" — about equally dusty, B. A asserts the very gap the swabs failed to find; the closing paragraph underlines it: "a difference in dirt that twenty-six machines failed to show". C misreads the machines — they were units "that had never burned", not new ones, and nothing is said about bare ducts. D is the sample-size dodge nobody in the piece makes: even Steadgrove, who "rejects nearly everything else", "accepts the swabs".

Grendisham's whole point is that the second timestamp records observation, not ignition: "On an unmanned site at two in the morning, that is when somebody looked out of a window, not when anything caught" — C. A inverts her argument; she says pairing the two numbers is what manufactures the apparent lateness ("Set those two numbers side by side and of course the fire looks late"). B confuses the fire department's log with her service book — the sixty-one files are the department's, county-wide. D is close in spirit but wrong in substance: she does not dismiss the log, she disputes what one of its columns means, and she reads the swabs evidentially too.

Steadgrove's date-sort implies the pressure in that window is general rather than machine-specific: "Sort the same sixty-one fires by date rather than by machine ... and the machine stops mattering. Forty-nine fall in a nine-day stretch at the tail of each harvest, when the deduction schedule bites hardest and the elevator's delivery window is closing" — A. B is a counting error: forty-nine of sixty-one, not all. C overshoots his own claim; he says the cause moves "to the contract", and the writer notes the schedule "belongs to the elevators", never that removing it would end the fires. D sounds right from "with trucks waiting", but that clause is a closing rhetorical scene about an operator's choice at 2 a.m.; no throughput or capacity shortfall is asserted anywhere.

The writer's verdict is a single sentence: "Until then Calverend's account fits the evidence without having been tested by it", preceded by "Grendisham's objection has not been answered, and it cannot be answered from files like these" — fits but untested, C. A cannot stand against "has not been answered". B is refuted by the fact that she adjudicates at all — she declares the dirt explanation dead ("nobody in the argument now defends it on the old ground"). D is the sharpest distractor, but the missing test needs "a probe inside a machine that later burns, and nobody has one", so she expects no confirmation next season; she only asks what the mutual should write into policy.

The gap completes the fixed idiom "take the long view", the tone set by the sentence before it: "which puts the bottom of the list twelve years from a key", and by "in the politest possible terms" — C. A is the near-synonym trap: "outlook" shares the sense of prospect but does not take "take the long ___"; one has a long-term outlook, one does not take one. B and D fail on both idiom and sense — "gaze" and "sight" are literal acts of looking, and neither carries the patience-with-a-slow-process meaning the paragraph needs.

The paragraph sets the written rule against the lived practice: "___, a plot cannot be inherited. The tenancy ends when the tenant does ... That is the clause as written ... It is simply not what the list runs on", which is the classic "Strictly, ..." concessive frame: B. C is pre-empted by the very next clause, "nobody disputes it or finds it odd" — the text denies the oddity that "Curiously" would assert. A needs a trend the passage never reports (the clause is stable, not increasingly true), and D would mean unofficially or in confidence, the opposite of a clause as written.

The sentence signposts a known phrase — "The older hands have a phrase for this among themselves, about waiting for dead men's ___" — and the idiom is "dead men's shoes", matching the context of movement only when somebody stops ("a knee that will not manage the walk from the gate"). B, C and D are all wearable items chosen to look parallel, but none is an English idiom, and the follow-up "It is not affectionate and it is not quite a joke" only makes sense of a phrase readers already recognise. "Gloves" is the most seductive of the three given all the digging, yet it names no waiting-for-a-vacancy expression at all.

The frame is a two-sided denial: "the tone of that line is not approving, but it is not ___ either", so the gap must hold the opposite pole of approval — disapproval, i.e. "censorious": D. A collapses the structure: "gracious" is on the approving side, so "not approving, but not gracious either" denies the same pole twice and says nothing. B and C name attitudes on an unrelated axis (care, worry); neither contrasts with approval, and neither fits minutes that "give it one line" about a tenancy transfer the committee tolerates without endorsing.

The rule exists on paper but has never been applied: "The rules say a second refusal sends a name to the foot of the list. The rule has not been ___" — "invoked" is the collocation for a rule being called upon: C. D is the sound-alike trap: "evoked" means to call up a feeling or memory and takes no rule as object. A would need a person or a meeting, not a clause, and B ("provoked") reverses the direction — a rule provokes a reaction, it is not itself provoked; the point is that three refusals passed without consequence.

The one diagnostic the writer endorses is height: "Height is the part worth reading. The pot that stands a course above its neighbours belongs to a flue that smoked, usually the shortest one on the stack" — a badly drawing flue, which is A. C inverts the passage's opening judgement, "Pattern tells you very little", and D is refuted by the same lines — yards "sold whatever was in stock" and ornament served "to tell their own door from thirty identical ones". B is the plausible real-world fact the text specifically does not give: the narrowing is explained aerodynamically, "since the same gases leave faster through less of an opening", with no mention of rain or birds.

The numbers only reconcile one way: the chandler's hatch "opened at seven in the morning and took in 412 letters; the bookseller's opened at two and took in 390", and "Both shut when the evening cart went at eight" — thirteen hours against six for a 22-letter difference, so volume tracks the cart's hour, not the hours open: D. B calls 412 versus 390 "far more", which the figures contradict. C is impossible because both shut at eight with the cart. A is the strongest wrong reading, since the keeper drew "threepence for every hour the hatch stood open, and not a penny for the letters themselves" — but the bookseller opened only at two, so no such stretching by both keepers is shown, and no motive is stated anywhere in the returns or the surveyor's note.
